column7: In D1 step 3, state that the adopt-only Add passes no Anchor and skips the source-dirt check, since an adopted live weft carries its own anchor and the fork point's dirt is not read when nothing is forked (internal/fabricengine/add.go:239-246 and 397-401 are the two refusals). Add a D1 acceptance criterion - a resume of a beam project's run whose task worktree is gone re-adopts its live pair at the anchor its weft records, and one with tracked dirt in the prime re-adopts too.

Replace D2's Land way forward with one that recovers a landed run whose pair is gone - for the not-live answer, name the step that restores the weft from its archive tag (or a new adopt-only add option over an archived weft, stated with its bound), and for each other permanent refusal class name the step that clears that refusal before the re-run. State how lym batten run treats the failed status at Land on the re-run, and change the D2 Land acceptance criterion to require that following the named steps resumes Land with the child's records present (PATTERN-refusal-way-forward - a test reaches the way forward).

Rewrite D1's first paragraph to say the tolerance is an option of the run scope that only batten's resume sets, under which the slug's entry is classified from its origin record and the Bolt without a pair worktree, and every other run-scope caller keeps today's error (internal/fabricengine/originreconcile.go:633, internal/fabricengine/destroy.go DropLocal). Keep the D1 acceptance criteria for the owned-elsewhere refusal and the absent-pair report.

In D2, list Add's refusal classes and the side each lands on - the not-live sentinel, the records-worktree-present refusal and ErrRemoteLeftover as permanent; a transport or probe failure, the D7 lock wait, a worktree-add failure and the anchor-move stop as transient - and state that Add wraps its probe and transport failures in a sentinel the pre-run tests with errors.Is. Add an acceptance criterion for one transient local refusal leaving the status running.

column6: _lym/discussion/decision-record.md D3 rule, rationale and fabric remove warning
column7: Correct D3's rationale to read that childReachedParent returns true only at Worktree-Teardown or past the parent-side merge (internal/battencli/cancel.go:691-708). Restrict D3's appended cancel and fabric remove's warning to a batten record standing before Land, and at Land name D2's corrected Land way forward instead. Add a D3 acceptance criterion - lym fabric remove of a slug whose batten record stands at Land does not name lym batten cancel.

In D3, state what the Finalize stop names after lym fabric remove given that the cancel's LiftPauses lifts every slug-scope pause including the owner pause (internal/battencli/cancelcmd.go liftSlugPauses) and refuses with cancelOwnedElsewhere when the local board shows another owner - either drop the appended cancel from this stop and leave the record to the adopt that clears the owner pause, or keep it and drop leaving the owner pause standing from the stop text. Add an acceptance criterion for the chosen behaviour.

In D6, name the lease as origin's weft tip after D4's branch push - the local tip when that push landed, else the tip D4 step 1 read - and state that D4 archives exactly that tip. Add a D6 acceptance criterion - a removal whose weft tip origin lacked pushes it and then deletes the weft branch on origin under the lease.

Extend D4's archive rule to the cleanup sweep in D6 - the sweep reads the weft branch's origin tip under the slug's teardown lock, archives it as well when it is neither the local tip nor an ancestor of it, and leases the remote delete on it (internal/fabricengine/cleanup.go:243-258, internal/fabricengine/archive.go resolveArchiveTip). Add a sweep acceptance criterion for an orphan whose origin tip diverges from the local one.

Research both now and record the answers with their evidence in Decisions or Constraints - for 2026-11-03, trace from the code what makes a new pair's weft branch read gone at a pass's bootstrap (internal/fabricengine/pushclassified.go checkOrigin and ErrBranchGone for a branch with an upstream origin lacks, the reconcile's BranchGone verdict, Add's step-11 leased replace of an archived leftover) and read this hub's run logs, then either design for the trigger found or state why D6 and D7 cover it; for missing necessary objects, cite git's receive-pack connectivity check from its docs at the version in use and state which cause D4's branch-first push and retry cover. Then drop both Open risks lines.
In D1's adopt-only option, state that a local weft branch whose tip an archive/<slug>/* tag covers also answers not-live, or reword the bound to name that case as one D1 re-adopts.
In D4 step 3, state that the diverged origin tip is fetched by SHA before its archive tag is made, as resolveArchiveTip already fetches an origin-only tip.

In D5, have the rule read the remote tip with git ls-remote and treat the named commit as present when it equals that tip or is an ancestor of it by git merge-base --is-ancestor where the tip is known locally, and as unsettled otherwise, never absent. Extend the D5 acceptance criterion to cover the ancestor case.

In D7's Bound, state the hold D4 can reach (one branch push plus the archive-tag retries, about a minute) against the teardown wait, and either size Add's and the discard's wait to cover it or state that a hand add or discard refused this way names the re-run.

Replace the first D7 acceptance criterion with one where Add of the slug waits while Remove, the discard or the sweep of the slug holds the teardown lock exclusive, then makes the pair once it is released.

In D1's Bound, state that it ends the rule that only the --adopt-local flag sets AdoptLocal (internal/fabricengine/add.go AddOptions.AdoptLocal, internal/fabricengine/doc.go, internal/fabriccli/doc.go) and replaces it with D1's rule that only the adopt-only resume sets it otherwise.

In 14-agent-gate-calls.md, add `internal/loomshed#verifyLineFindings` under **Edit:** and `//internal/loomshed/doc.go` under **Uses:**. Its Intent also rewrites loom-plan-spec.md's gate-keys sentence (line 320): a Go site runs `lym gate test --wait --gate <key>`, and an agent's card, batch and `webster-fix` calls carry no `--wait`. It rewrites the `verify-gate-no-wait` reason (line 595) and the Detail of the `verifyGateNoWaitCheck` finding in verifyLineFindings to the reason that holds: Go re-runs the line outside an agent hook, and a gate call without `--wait` is a slot-held line, run inside one slot under the card-verify runner's timeout instead of taking its tiers' own slots.

In 11-gate-capped-front.md's Choice (D2) paragraph, add a Bound sentence: an in-process call now waits for its slots without a cap, ended only when a holder releases its slots, each holder's run being bounded by its tier's `timeout_min`, or by the caller's own interrupt, which cancels the wait and exits 1 as today.

In 13-card-verify-capped.md's runner paragraph, add: when the matched card has no `**Verify:**` line in the runner's read, the runner writes the in-process ok envelope (`card <id> has no **Verify:** line; nothing to run`) to `stdout` and an unmarked exit `{Code: 0}`, so the front replays it as the in-process verb answers.

In 11-gate-capped-front.md's Tests paragraph, say that helperLaunch under `none` writes a fixed line, such as `gate helper: the runner was never started`, to the run's `runner.log` before it returns the ended process's pid, and the `none` row asserts that line on the front's stderr.
